synopsis: ISO/TC 127 is the technical committee for earth-moving machinery and produces nearly every off-road standard covered by the booklet, including collision systems, detection, brakes, functional safety, autonomous machines and machine definitions [f15033, f15034]. Standard numbers, parts and years identify specific documents and editions; each part has its own scope and date, while prefixes distinguish document types and national or regional adoptions [f15033, f15036, f15040, f15041]. ISO 21815 covers earth-moving machines defined in ISO 6165, underground mining machines under ISO 19296, and road-construction machines [f15140]. An older edition year does not itself imply obsolescence: ISO 16001’s current edition is 2017, and ISO 3450:2011 was reviewed and confirmed in 2022 [f15037, f15038]. All five ISO 19014 parts change in October 2026, so the program should baseline the editions actually published rather than mix clauses from different years; ISO 21815-4 should not be cited as published until its text appears [f15039, f15042, f15043]. The booklet found no ISO/TC 127 study applying road-vehicle simulation methods to off-road machines, with the chapter-level search also reporting no such study across several other organizations [f1698, f15035].
